threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think all the coffee shops serve 'regular' sizes instead of 'small,' 'medium,' and 'large.' It’s a tell.
Last week, a guy was trying to impress his date on the bus, turned up the radio on his phone, only to get busted by the driver for noise. Awkward silence followed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: That moment when you realize the kebab shop staff know your order by heart, and you can hear their banter through the window while you wait.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Kebab shop that doubles as a punk music venue at midnight. Gritty, loud, and deliciously unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they casually mention the smell of burnt toast from the BART tube—just part of the commute, not a surprise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus driver in the Tenderloin singing along to the radio, completely unbothered by the chaos around. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the 'pommes frites' at the kiosks are the local snack. True locals grab a 'bocata' from the corner bars instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their puzzled expressions at the bus stops, still trying to decipher the irregular schedules.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep asking for milk in pints instead of litres. You get confused when people don’t know what ‘the corner shop’ actually refers to.
Saw a guy in a tracksuit trying to sell a single roller skate on the 133 last night. No one even blinked. Just another night in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids playing football in the street while their grandparents sat on balcony chairs, sharing stories over strong coffee.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Ever notice how Kreuzberg's kebab shops stay open late? It’s the only place where you can grab a döner at 3 AM and chat with the owner like an old friend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can tell you which taco truck has the best lengua without hesitation, and it’s always at 16th and Mission.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy eat a whole burrito on the 19 Polk, sauce dripping down his shirt, while arguing about the best taqueria. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals dine late, but many of us are already in bed by the time they start their meals. Early birds miss the nightlife buzz.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they still look at the metro map like it's a crossword puzzle, utterly lost but trying to act cool about it.
